explain.say: Here is a tricky question: if you have chatted with someone in a game every day for months, do you really know them? Look at the left side of the board: a friend you know. You have met them, and your parents know their family.

explain.say: Now look at the right side: an online-only friend. You have never met them, they could be anyone, and photos can be fake. A twelve-year-old gamer might really be an adult. Does that surprise you?

explain.say: So watch for warning signs, called red flags. Look at the first one: they ask you to keep secrets, like, do not tell your parents. That is a big red flag. Why do you think that is?

faq.q: What are warning signs from someone online?
faq.a: Red flags include asking you to keep secrets, asking for photos, wanting to meet, giving gifts, asking personal questions, or making you feel special and then pressured.
asks: Tell me about the Asks for secrets
How do I know if someone online is lying?

faq.q: Will I get in trouble if I tell?
faq.a: No. Telling a trusted adult is always the right thing, even if you broke an app rule or already sent something. Adults want to help you.
asks: Tell me about the Tell a trusted adult

faq.q: Should I meet someone I met online?
faq.a: Never go alone. If you want to meet, talk to a parent or carer first; they decide and come with you to a public place.
asks: Tell me about the Wants to meet

faq.q: Is it safe to talk to people I meet in games?
faq.a: Keep chats about the game, never share personal information, use privacy settings, and tell an adult if anyone makes you uncomfortable.
asks: Can I chat in online games?

faq.q: What should I do if someone asks for a photo?
faq.a: Say no, stop chatting, block and report them, and tell a trusted adult straight away. It is never your fault.
asks: Tell me about the Asks for photos

facts: Child-safety organisations advise that children should never meet someone they only know online without a parent or carer.
People online can use fake names, ages and photos, so you cannot be sure who someone really is.
